description: workspace_switch writes the active workspace id to the KV key 'workspace.active' (line 1596), but every other component reads the active workspace from the 'active_space_id' field embedded inside the 'workspaces' JSON blob. The orchestrator's active_space_scope (orchestrator.rs:728) reads active_space_id from the workspaces blob; KanbanBackend::get_active_workspace_id (kanban.rs:166) reads active_space_id from the workspaces blob; the frontend (frontend/src/stores/workspace.rs:73) stores active_space_id inside WorkspaceState and persists the whole struct to the 'workspaces' key via save(). As a result, when an LLM uses the workspace_switch tool, it successfully writes 'workspace.active' — a key nothing else ever reads for determining the active space — so the orchestrator state snapshot, the Kanban backend, and the frontend all continue to show the old workspace as active. The switch silently fails. Fix: update workspace_switch to mutate the 'active_space_id' field inside the 'workspaces' JSON blob (read, parse, set active_space_id, serialize, write-back) and remove the separate 'workspace.active' key, or have all reading sites also consult 'workspace.active' consistently.

In search_code, the context_after Vec for each SearchMatch is initialized as empty (line 213) and never populated during the match processing loop (lines 216-223 only push to context_before). Context lines that appear AFTER a match are only assigned to the very last match in the results, at lines 247-258, after the main loop ends. For all non-last matches, context_after is permanently empty — the 'after' context lines ripgrep emitted are silently dropped from the SearchMatch struct even though they were captured in pending_context. This means code_search results show before-context but never after-context for all but the final match. Fix: after pushing a new match at line 233, check whether the NEXT match's line_num is within context_lines_count and, if the next match is far enough, scan pending_context for after-lines belonging to this match; or restructure to buffer context lines between matches and assign after-context when the next match (or end-of-stream) is seen.

In SwarmCoordinator::send_message, the mailbox is read with serde_json::from_str(&content).unwrap_or_default() (line 236). If the mailbox file contains malformed JSON — e.g. it was partially written during a crash, or truncated by a filesystem error — this silently returns an empty Vec, discarding all previously-stored unread messages. The new message is then pushed onto the empty list and the whole thing is renamed over the mailbox (line 255), permanently destroying all prior unread messages. The same silent-swallow pattern appears in read_mailbox (line 280), where ALL filesystem errors (not just NotFound) return Ok(Vec::new()), masking permission errors and corruption. Fix: on parse failure, rename the corrupt file to a .corrupt sidecar (preserving data for forensic recovery) and start fresh, or return an error so the caller knows messages were lost; for read_mailbox, distinguish NotFound (→ empty) from other IO/parse errors (→ Err).

send_anthropic (line 1317) uses the hardcoded Anthropic API version header '2024-10-22', while one_title_call (line 1131) uses the ANTHROPIC_VERSION constant ('2023-06-01', defined at line 17). These two code paths talk to the same Anthropic Messages API but advertise different API versions, which can cause subtly different behavior in error responses, rate-limit headers, and feature availability. Fix: use ANTHROPIC_VERSION (or a single updated constant) consistently in both send_anthropic and one_title_call, or extract a shared helper that builds the Anthropic request headers.

The doc comment block at lines 38-41 ('Maximum size in bytes of a single agent-comms line...') is a near-verbatim duplicate of the correct comment at lines 11-15 (which precedes the MAX_AGENT_LINE_BYTES const). The duplicate at line 38 is misplaced: it appears immediately before the AgentMessageType enum, with which it has nothing to do. A reader will be confused by a line-size comment attached to a message-type enum. Fix: delete the duplicate comment block at lines 38-42.

In append_output, the condition `if raw_line.is_empty() && raw_lines.len() > 1 { continue; }` (line 341-343) drops ALL empty lines from any output chunk that contains more than one line. This is presumably intended to strip the spurious trailing empty string produced by split('
') on a trailing newline, but it also strips meaningful blank lines inside the output — e.g. paragraph breaks in agent text ("Step 1 done.

Step 2 starting.") lose the blank separator, corrupting the rendered and persisted output. Fix: only strip the trailing empty string (if raw_lines.last() is Some("") and the raw_data ended with '
'), not interior empty lines; or use split_terminator('
') which does not produce a trailing empty string.
